annotations.title: Is this city's housing supply keeping up with its rent and population?

description: Use when the user is weighing a housing, zoning, development or site decision for a US city, or checking a claim about one: "is Boise building enough housing?", "how fast has rent risen in St. Paul against the country?", "did permits in Austin fall after 2022?". Returns population, households, median rent, median income, rent burden and work-from-home share in 2019 and 2023-2025 beside the US, and new housing units permitted each year from 2015 to 2025 (all and in 5+ unit buildings), per 1,000 residents, from US Census Bureau data. Cities of 65,000+ residents that file their own permits. Refuses before you are charged if the city cannot be matched, its permits are filed by another office, or its permit file is not believable (a large city reporting no apartment permits, or far below its county). Describes; takes no side on any policy. Every result carries a run id, a date and a citation line. Calling this tool returns a quote, not the result: what the run measures, its price and a payment_url. The run happens only when you POST to payment_url, and a run that fails its controls refuses there with nothing charged. Price: $0.05 per run over x402 (USDC on Base, no account needed), or $0.50 over MPP (a Stripe shared payment token); charged only when the run comes back sound.
